item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 031717
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sat Oct 3 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Nolo, located several hundred miles west-northwest of the main
Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Rachel, located a few hundred
miles south-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form late this weekend or
early next week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is likely to form during the middle to
latter portion of next week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Public Advisory Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Sat Oct 03 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 031435
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM MST Sat Oct 03 2026
 
...RACHEL MOVING SLOWLY WEST-NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.6N 112.1W
ABOUT 270 MI...430 KM SSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...85 MPH...140 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...973 MB...28.74 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 19.6 North, longitude 112.1 West. Rachel is moving
toward the west-northwest near 3 mph (6 km/h), and this slow motion 
is expected to continue through tonight.  A west to west-northwest 
motion is then expected Sunday through the middle of next week, 
with a gradual increase in forward speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 85 mph (140 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Some weakening is forecast during the next day 
or so, with some slight restrengthening possible on Monday. Rachel 
is forecast to remain a hurricane for the next few days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 973 mb (28.74 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will continue to affect the coast 
of west-central Mexico through the weekend and the Baja California 
Peninsula through Monday. These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult 
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Sat Oct 03 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 031437
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM MST Sat Oct 03 2026
 
Rachel's convective structure has gradually become less impressive 
over past day.  Satellite imagery shows the deep convection nearly 
void in the northwest quadrant, which is likely allowing some dry 
air to entrain into the center of Rachel.  The latest subjective 
Dvorak current intensity number from TAFB is 4.5/77 kt.  Recent 
objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 65-72 kt.  
The initial intensity is lowered to 75 kt for this advisory.

Rachel is now moving slowly west-northwestward, or 290 degrees at 3 
kt.  A mid- to upper-level anticyclone over the western United 
States has a ridge extending southwest out in front of Rachel's 
path.  Rachel is expected to continue moving quite slowly for the 
next 2 days as the ridge remains in place to Rachel's 
west-northwest.  Early next week, a mid- to upper-level trough to 
the west of the ridge will very gradually strengthen and drift 
eastward, which will slowly erode the ridge over the 3- to 5-day 
time period.  This will allow Rachel to gain some forward speed by 
hour 60, with a continued motion between west and west-northwest.  
The NHC track forecast is slightly north of the previous track 
through 60 h, and slightly south of the previous official track at 
days 4-5. The NHC forecast is in good agreement with the latest HFIP 
Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA), and lies slightly to the south 
of the latest Google DeepMind Ensemble Mean through 96 h.  It should 
be noted that there is a fair amount of north-south (cross-track) 
spread in the guidance, and forecast confidence appears to be near 
average.

Additional gradual weakening is forecast during the next 24 hours as 
sea-surface temperatures (SSTs) decrease along Rachel's path while 
the cyclone moves over the cold water wake left over by Hurricane 
Polo last week.  After Rachel emerges out of Polo's cold wake, some 
slight restrengthening is expected, and this restrengthening is 
shown in the HAFS-A, HAFS-B, and HWRF models.  Beyond hour 72, 
Rachel will reach dry mid-level air with relative humidity values 
near 40 percent.  SSTs will also be decreasing at that time, and 
Rachel is expected to cross the 26C degree SST isotherm in about 4 
days.  The NHC forecast continues to show weakening in the 3- to 
5-day time frame due to the drier air and cooling SSTs.  The NHC 
intensity forecast is still near the high end of the guidance 
envelope through the first 4 days and closer to the middle of the 
guidance envelope by day 5.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 24H  04/1200Z 20.2N 113.7W   65 KT  75 MPH
